To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of a double mitochondrial targeting sequence improves the delivery of GFP probes into the matrix; 2) the use of the same targeting sequence can affect the fluorescent properties and Ca2+ affinity; and 3) the targeting sequence can be easily removed from the imported probe by a proteolytic cleavage site.

(i) the efficiency of mitochondrial import is a key factor that determines the overall performance of the probe in the matrix, and that (ii) the targeting signal should not be left attached to the imported protein.

(1) the choice of targeting signal can influence not only the overall delivery efficiency of the probe into the organelles, but also the functional characteristics of the probe within the organelles and (2) if the targeting sequence remains attached to the imported proteins, it affects the functional properties of the protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel strategies that can improve the targeting and the functional properties of GFP-based Ca(2+) probes to the mitochondrial matrix.

the development of improved strategies for the delivery into the mitochondrial matrix of the latest generation Ca2+ probes, which will be useful for studying Ca2+ dynamics and its role in mitochondrial physiology.
the development of new and improved methods for the study of mitochondrial Ca2+.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice of the targeting sequence is crucial for the correct delivery of the probe into the organelles, and for its functional properties.
the choice of mitochondrial targeting sequence is crucial in determining the subcellular localization and functional properties of GFP-based Ca(2+) probes.

Cameleon, when targeted to the matrix with the use of a single mitochondrial targeting sequence, shows the best performance in terms of Ca2+ sensitivity, Ca2+-induced changes in fluorescence, kinetics of response and Ca2+-independent fluorescence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of tandemly duplicated mitochondrial-targeting sequence can improve the efficiency of delivery of the GFP-based Ca2+-sensors into the mitochondrial matrix and the removal of the targeting sequence is necessary to avoid interference with the fluorescent properties of the probes.
the choice of the targeting sequence is critical for the delivery of Cameleon into the mitochondria, but not for Camgaroo or Pericam.

the use of tandemly repeated targeting sequences is a useful tool for the improvement of subcellular targeting, and that the removal of the targeting sequence from the imported protein should be performed as early as possible to avoid unwanted side effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of tandemly duplicated mitochondrial matrix targeting sequence can improve the targeting of GFP-based Ca(2+) sensors into the organelles matrix and that the removal of the targeting sequence is essential to maintain the functional characteristics of the imported protein.
a careful choice of targeting sequence is crucial for the successful delivery of Ca2+ probes into the mitochondrial matrix.
a combination of the two strategies (tandem duplication of the mitochondrial targeting sequence, and removal of the targeting sequence) can be used for the delivery of any GFP-based Ca2+.
